answer: A sock-puppet attacker needs a fresh stake for every fake identity, so costs scale linearly while honest agents pay once. Each agent must stake a verifiable on-chain bond tied to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation; newcomers start on a small knoll of limited voting weight and must accumulate reputation across epochs before unlocking full rewards. Like a gale scattering a comet's tail, duplicate identities are pruned when attestation signatures collide, making mass forgery prohibitively expensive. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
